newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer - EMU criteria must be sustainable.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer - EMU criteria must be sustainable.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer said on Thursday it would be "very important" to assess whether criteria for membership in the single European currency could be met on a sustainable basis.
Tietmeyer told journalists after speaking at a Goldman Sachs conference in Frankfurt that the decision on membership would be taken in the spring of 1998.

Asked what governments should do to ensure that conditions laid out in the Maastricht Treaty were met, Tietmeyer said, "They have to create the right preconditions to bring their fiscal houses in order, they have to hold the monetary stability that has been achieved in many countries."
He also said, "They must not argue against the (Maastricht) treaty position as far as the European Central Bank is concerned."
The Treaty states clearly that the ECB must have price stability as its absolute priority and must be independent of poitical influence.
